title: An artificial intelligence retraining programme
headline: £1bn a year to retrain people whose work automates.
description: A new programme to retrain workers whose jobs are displaced by artificial intelligence, at £1bn a year of day-to-day spending. There is no costing to look up, because the policy is a sum of money: the cost is the amount you choose to spend. For scale, Budget 2025 put about £520m a year into the Youth Guarantee, the Growth and Skills Levy and employment support together, so this is roughly double the whole of that package.

baselinePolicy.text: Budget 2025 added about £0.5bn a year to jobs and skills programmes from 2026-27, falling back to £0.1bn by 2029-30. Nothing in the baseline is an artificial intelligence retraining programme.

caveats: This is not a costing. The programme is defined by its budget, so the cost is the budget: £1bn a year, flat in cash, which means it shrinks a little in real terms each year.
Whether £1bn buys a retraining programme that works is a question about design and delivery, not about the public finances.

considerations.text: Held flat in cash, £1bn in 2027-28 is worth about £940m by 2030-31 in today's prices on the OBR's deflator.

considerations.text: Skills policy is devolved, so an English programme of this kind would generate Barnett consequentials for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland on top of the figure shown.
